title: GELDA: A generative language annotation framework to reveal visual biases in datasets

bias_targets.methodology: Using Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate environmental and contextual attributes (e.g., habitat, location, background scenery) and Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to zero-shot annotate images, identifying confounding correlations between dataset class labels and these background features (e.g., waterbirds with coastal backgrounds, luxury cars with parking lots).

Generating domain-specific lists of visual attributes (e.g., room color schemes, furniture presence, dog postures) via an LLM and annotating synthetic images generated by text-to-image models to detect heavily skewed or uneven attribute distributions.

Using the LLM/VLM annotation framework to label synthetic human faces for physical and demographic attributes (e.g., skin tone, perceived age, gender, hair color, facial expression) and comparing the generated attribute frequencies against the training dataset distributions to measure bias amplification.
